title: Internal-composition equations for normalized coefficient reduction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an arbitrary scheme $W$ in an independent universe, and a coefficient fiber calculus $S$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. Let $R$ be its explicit normalized reduction data [def-pur-canonical-coefficient-reduction]. For its reduction functor, and for each finite scalar-extension functor, the evaluation-defined base-change map preserves internal composition. Explicitly, for the relevant closed structures $A,B$, functor $F$ and conjugated tensor comparison $\mu$, and all derived inputs $P,Q,V$, one has $F(\operatorname{comp}_A(P,Q,V));\beta(P,V)=\mu_{[Q,V],[P,Q]};(\beta(Q,V)\otimes\beta(P,Q));\operatorname{comp}_B(FP,FQ,FV)$. Here composition is transposed iterated evaluation with the specified normalized associator, and $\beta$ is transposed reduced evaluation [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. This is solely two families of morphism equations: it asserts no existence of a calculus, fiber-Hom comparison, enriched adjunction, or global comparison.

proof.text: For any fixed closed structure on a ringed site, prove uniqueness of its CoefficientTensorModels. For K-flat P,L put M=Tot(P tensor L) and curry the identity of M by the existing chain tensor-Hom equivalence. The normalized_uncurry equation for each of two models says that its comparison followed by the same derived inverse transpose z is Q(identity_M). Thus z is the inverse of either comparison, so their components agree. Natural-transformation extensionality and proof irrelevance give equality of the models. This uses no coherence hypothesis and no claim that a general adjoint comparison preserves associators.

proof.text: The integral, sequence and finite closed structures of the explicit normalized reduction R are the fixed RingedSiteDualityModel.closed structures. Apply model uniqueness to identify each transported tensor model with that duality model's own model. Its proved ringedSiteTensorCoherence supplies full tensor coherence; transport along the model equality and assemble CoefficientDerivedSystemTensorCoherence for R.

Apply coefficientNormalizedTensorAssociativity with the coherence just proved to obtain both inverse-comparison associativity families for the actual conjugated tensor maps. The strict-system calculation and its localization are supplied by that existing tensor-only theorem, rather than by a new composition split.

proof.text: Apply the proved generic baseChange_composition calculation of CoefficientNormalizedInternalHomFibers to each associativity family. That calculation uncurries both sides, uses evaluation naturality and inverse-comparison associativity, then transposes back and cancels the inverse tensor comparison. Its conclusion is definitionally CompositionLaw. Pair the reduction conclusion with the family of finite conclusions. No fiber-Hom existence or global-sections theorem is used.

theorem compositionLaws (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemFibers l E W) :
    let R := reduction l E W S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
    CompositionLaw R.integralClosed R.systemClosed R.reduction R.reductionTensor ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, CompositionLaw R.integralClosed (R.finiteClosed n)
        (coefficientFiniteDerivedExtension l E W n) (R.finiteTensor n)
